grammarFocus: 比较结构、数量表达与指代综合；冠词和主谓一致检查。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. Preserve a coherent new scenario; do not rename an earlier text, reuse its facts or reveal answers in question stems.

title: How a City Library Makes Expert Knowledge Accessible
instructions: 本材料为模拟练习，不是官方雅思考试，也不对应任何官方分数。先听录音（或阅读文字稿），完成10道听力题；再学习语法讲解并完成8道语法题；最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。听力题中，填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for coming to this short tour. I’m Maya, and I coordinate the public programs here at the Northside Library. Today I want to show you how we make expert knowledge accessible to ordinary residents.

Daniel: Sorry to interrupt—did you say “expert knowledge”? What does that mean exactly?

Maya: Good question. It means we invite specialists—doctors, engineers, lawyers—to explain their work in simple language. We don’t expect people to have university degrees. Last year we ran forty-two workshops, and more than six hundred people attended. That’s twice as many as the year before.

Daniel: Wow. So who pays for these workshops?

Maya: The city gives us a small grant, but most of the money comes from volunteers. We have about thirty regular volunteers, and they help with everything from setting up chairs to translating handouts into Chinese and Spanish.

Priya: I’m Priya, by the way. I’m a nurse, and I came to one of your health talks last month. I found it really useful. But I noticed the room was quite full—maybe too full?

Maya: You’re right. The health talk was the most popular event we’ve ever had. We had to turn away almost fifty people because the room only holds eighty. So next month we’re moving the big talks to the community hall, which seats two hundred and fifty.

Priya: That’s a big improvement. Will you still keep the small workshops?

Maya: Yes, definitely. The small ones are for hands-on practice—for example, a session on how to read a medical report. Those work best with fewer than twenty people. The large talks are more like lectures, with a question-and-answer session at the end.

Daniel: Do you record the talks? I sometimes can’t come in the evening.

Maya: We do now. Since January we’ve posted every talk online, and each video has been watched at least three hundred times. Some have been watched more than a thousand times. The online audience is actually larger than the in-person audience.

Priya: That’s interesting. But not everyone has internet at home.

Maya: Exactly. That’s why we also keep printed summaries at the front desk. They’re free, and they’re written in plain English. We print five hundred copies of each summary, and they usually disappear within two weeks.

Daniel: So the library is becoming more like a community classroom?

Maya: That’s a nice way to put it. Our goal is simple: fewer barriers, more access. Anyone with a library card can join—no fees, no tests, no prior knowledge required.

Priya: I’ll definitely tell my colleagues about this.

Maya: Please do. And if either of you wants to volunteer, we always need more help. The next training session is on the first Saturday of next month, at ten in the morning.

grammar.title: 比较结构、数量表达与指代综合；冠词和主谓一致检查
grammar.explanation: 本课重点是比较结构、数量表达和指代的一致性。比较结构如“twice as many as”“more than”“fewer than”“the most popular”等，要注意比较对象和数量词搭配。数量表达如“forty-two workshops”“six hundred people”“three hundred times”等，要区分具体数字和概数。指代要明确，如“The small ones”指代前面的“small workshops”，“They”指代“printed summaries”。冠词方面，特指用the，泛指用a/an或零冠词；主谓一致要注意主语和谓语在人称和数上一致，如“The city gives”“volunteers help”“each video has been watched”。
grammar.example: Last year we ran forty-two workshops, and more than six hundred people attended. That’s twice as many as the year before.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The new hall seats ______ people than the old room.
questions.explanation: 比较级用more，表示“更多”，与than搭配。
questions.evidence: So next month we’re moving the big talks to the community hall, which seats two hundred and fifty.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: This year we have ______ volunteers than last year.
questions.explanation: volunteers是可数名词复数，比较级用fewer，不用less。
questions.evidence: We have about thirty regular volunteers, and they help with everything from setting up chairs to translating handouts into Chinese and Spanish.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The health talk was ______ popular event we’ve ever had.
questions.explanation: 最高级前加the，表示“最受欢迎的”。
questions.evidence: The health talk was the most popular event we’ve ever had.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: ______ video has been watched at least three hundred times.
questions.explanation: each后接单数名词，谓语用has been watched，主谓一致。
questions.evidence: Since January we’ve posted every talk online, and each video has been watched at least three hundred times.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The library ______ free printed summaries at the front desk.
questions.explanation: 主语The library是单数，谓语用keeps，保持主谓一致。
questions.evidence: That’s why we also keep printed summaries at the front desk.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The volunteers ______ with setting up chairs and translating handouts.
questions.explanation: 主语The volunteers是复数，谓语用help，保持主谓一致。
questions.evidence: We have about thirty regular volunteers, and they help with everything from setting up chairs to translating handouts into Chinese and Spanish.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: We print five hundred ______ of each summary.
questions.explanation: five hundred后接可数名词复数copies。
questions.evidence: We print five hundred copies of each summary, and they usually disappear within two weeks.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The small workshops are for hands-on practice; ______ work best with fewer than twenty people.
questions.explanation: 指代前面的The small workshops，用they作主语。
questions.evidence: The small ones are for hands-on practice—for example, a session on how to read a medical report. Those work best with fewer than twenty people.
